title: Electricity Generation by Source (Daily, CEA)
description: Daily all-India electricity generation by fuel from the Central Electricity Authority's Daily Generation Report (sub-report 17), in million units (MU = GWh) net of auxiliary use, for stations above 25 MW: coal, lignite, natural gas, nuclear, hydro, and imports from Bhutan. It EXCLUDES wind, solar and other small renewables (see the daily renewable generation indicator). Daily coal-fired output tracks industrial and household power demand almost in real time, which makes it one of the fastest read-throughs on activity; hydro and gas swing with the monsoon and fuel availability. The monthly view takes CEA's own month-to-date figure on the last day of the month (or the sum of the days where every day is present).
source: Central Electricity Authority (National Power Portal), Daily Generation Report

views.label: Daily total YoY % (same date last year)

qna.question: What does this measure?
qna.answer: Actual generation on the day, in million units (MU), for all grid-connected thermal (coal, lignite, gas, diesel/naphtha), nuclear and hydro stations above 25 MW, plus imports from Bhutan. Rooftop and small solar/wind and other renewables are not in this file.^MU is the same as GWh; 4,000 MU a day is an average load of about 167 GW.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Daily figures swing with weekdays, weather and the monsoon, so look at the YoY view and the monthly view for trend. Coal generation is the swing producer: when demand outruns renewables and hydro, coal output rises, so it is the cleanest daily read on underlying power demand. A cool or rainy spell lowers coal output even when activity is unchanged.^This is a flow measured over the period, so compare it with the same period a year ago (the YoY view) rather than with the previous period.

qna.question: Definitions, revisions and caveats
qna.answer: Each day is taken from that day's CEA report ('Today's Actual'); CEA files are produced the next afternoon and some days can be revised in later cumulative figures, so very recent days are provisional. A few days are missing from the CEA archive (the file was never published) and are left blank, not filled in.^The monthly series uses the report's own month-to-date total on the last day of the month; it can differ slightly from CEA's final monthly generation statistics, which include later corrections. Because renewables are excluded, the total understates all-India generation (renewables are roughly a fifth of annual energy).
